calls.title: Onboarding: Intro, Company History & Purpose, Product Demo
calls.summary: GrowthBook was founded to transform the traditional software development cycle by promoting faster, data-driven experimentation, addressing a $600 billion problem of failed product changes. With insights from Graham McNicoll, it was noted that only 20-33% of experiments succeed, highlighting the necessity for a solution. The platform is open-source and has gained over 7,000 stars on GitHub, serving over 2,800 companies, growing organically without marketing. The core mission emphasizes quick building, measuring, and iterating to avoid costly failures. GrowthBook's modular design targets engineering, data science, and product leadership, enabling self-service experimentation while maintaining trust and accuracy. The company operates with a flat, remote-first culture that encourages transparency and autonomy, with a robust onboarding process for new hires.
calls.keywords: Experimentation, A/B Testing, Onboarding, Product Development, GrowthBook, Remote Work

calls.title: Onboarding: Intro, Company History & Purpose, Product Demo
calls.summary: Growth Book aims to transform the software release process with a data-driven feedback loop that enhances developer efficiency and product improvements. Last year, the company generated $7.8 million in revenue primarily from 2,800 enterprise customers, and recently secured $13 million in Series A funding, ensuring over five years of runway for sustainable growth. Their open-source platform promotes transparency and customization, supporting various tech stacks through 24 SDKs. The sales team is expanding to enhance customer engagement, supported by a dedicated customer success team focused on long-term relationships. The company's culture emphasizes humility and collaboration, fostering an environment where continuous learning and experimentation are prioritized.
